title: Commit only when asked, and the sealed guard's second review
request: Stop hook: every R&D agent behind the chat and the parity plan's open items; owner: do not wait for me.
spec: dclab-code docs/PARITY_PLAN.md (open from the live tests), server/prompts/system_append.md, server/guards.js, server/config.js
plan: check the parity table against R&D's AGENTS list (18 of 18 reached, sync-check)
close the open items: the commit rule, Edit/Write live, a second review of the sealed guard
fix the review's findings, review the fixes, fix again

decisions.decision: git is asked which files a git command prints (names only) instead of refusing every git show and diff
decisions.why: git show and git diff are routine; refusing them would be a false ask on most turns, while names-only is exact

decisions.decision: names-only commands (find without -exec, du, ls, wc, tree) no longer ask
decisions.why: they print names and sizes, never a row; repo-wide exploration asked on nearly every find in R&D

decisions.decision: base64 and other deliberate obfuscation stay out of scope
decisions.why: string matching cannot stop them; R&D's read-once records are the backstop

change: dclab-code 4a54413 (commit rule, parity plan), 671fe84 (second review fixes), 7b433e5 (fixes of the fix review).

findings.defect: the system prompt never said to leave commits to the person
findings.scenario: Opus committed unasked in a live test
findings.fix: commit, push or open a pull request only when the person asks
findings.test: live: Sonnet 5.5 fixed calc.py with Edit, ran the test, committed nothing ($0.12)

findings.defect: git show of a commit that adds a sealed set printed it unasked
findings.cause: a revision never names 'sealed'; show/log/diff were not checked
findings.fix: run git with --name-only on the same command and ask on a sealed name; a blob by id and cat-file -p ask
findings.test: units: git show/log -p/format-patch/cat-file of the sealed commit ask; git show HEAD of code passes

findings.defect: inline code listing a sealed folder passed
findings.cause: no glob or recursive flag; scripts were read only when run from a file
findings.fix: inlineReason checks folders named in -c/-e code, here-docs and $(...), and a cd into a sealed folder

findings.defect: R&D's sealed runs called directly or quoted passed
findings.scenario: python -m dclab_rnd.agent_eval.benchmark --split test; make benchmark SPLIT='test'
findings.cause: plain substring match on the raw command
findings.fix: match on shell words with spaces collapsed; module forms added
each letter written as a class

findings.defect: the fix ran a program inside the guard
findings.scenario: git -c core.fsmonitor='touch x' diff HEAD~1 created x before any ask
findings.cause: the person's -c options were passed to the guard's own git run
findings.fix: ask for any git command with its own settings; run git with hooks, fsmonitor and external diff off
findings.test: units: the mark file is never made

findings.defect: the fix's false-ask cuts opened bypasses
findings.scenario: git show ':/msg', git commit -F sealed, grep -e. sealed, find "-exec" cat, git add -p, cat-file --batch=FMT, git archive
findings.cause: ':' read as rev:path, -F skipped as a message, attached flag values, raw-string regex

findings.scenario: git show with 200 revisions held the server 3.7 s
findings.fix: at most 6 git runs within 6 s a step, then ask
findings.test: units: 200 revisions ask in under 1.5 s

findings.defect: git ignored the guard's flags after --
findings.cause: flags appended after the person's args; after -- every word is a path

measurements.name: tests
measurements.result: dclab-code 150 of 150 (units 53, page 31 on rerun after one load timeout)

measurements.name: review inputs
measurements.gate: every bypass the reviews named asks
measurements.result: all ask but deliberate obfuscation (base64, a script written then run without a sealed name in it) and ':/msg' resolving to a commit without sealed files (correct)

measurements.name: false asks
measurements.result: find | wc, du -sh *, ls globs, wc -l, commit messages, git add, grep words, pytest -k sealed, checksums now pass; reading docs or notebooks named holdout still asks

measurements.name: live
measurements.result: Read, Read, Edit, Bash test; no git commit; $0.125

outcome: The parity table covers all 18 R&D agents; the guard closes the git-history and inline-code holes and asks less on harmless exploration.
lessons: Ask the tool that owns the data (git) what a command would print, rather than guessing from its words.
Every false-ask cut is a new bypass until reviewed: review the fix, not only the bug.
A guard must never run anything the guarded command configures.
risks: Deliberate obfuscation still passes; the guard is a seatbelt, not a sandbox.
The owner has not yet confirmed the app in their own window.
